# Trellis For Rust Consumers

Use with [the consumer guide](llms-full.txt) from the same Trellis revision.
Trellis does not prescribe an application's configuration parser, database,
domain types, DI pattern, logging setup, or test framework.

## Generated Package

Author native IDL and set `format = 1` and a local package `name` such as
`orders-trellis` in `trellis.toml`. Root `Cargo.toml` selects Rust. A Rust-only
project defaults to `trellis/`, optionally overridden by `[generate].output`;
mixed-language projects require explicit Rust and TypeScript output tables.
`trellis generate` is offline after dependencies are available in the global
validated API cache.

The output is one ordinary crate at version `0.0.0`, with
`orders_trellis::apis::<api>` and `orders_trellis::participants::<participant>`
modules, not independent SDK or participant crates. Add an ordinary Cargo path
dependency, for example `orders-trellis = { path = "trellis" }`. The generated
crate declares the published runtime dependency matching the CLI. It has no
generator build script, repository-relative runtime paths, or runtime-path config
in `trellis.toml`. Use ordinary Cargo overrides when developing against a local
runtime. Generation does not modify the consumer's Cargo manifest.

Commit generated output when clones should build with Cargo alone, without the
Trellis CLI or API cache. Regenerate rather than editing it. Canonical tooling
JSON lives inside the package under `artifacts/apis` and `artifacts/participants`;
it is not a language import surface.

An API SDK contains types and descriptors. The participant facade supplies the
connection boundary and only the declared caller/provider surfaces. Its
constants carry participant/API evidence; applications do not supply those
digests to service bootstrap.

## Connection

Service facades export `connect` and `ServiceConnectOptions`. The current
constructor takes only Trellis URL and the provisioned identity seed; name and
timeout are optional builders:

```rust
let mut service = connect(
    ServiceConnectOptions::new(&trellis_url, &identity_seed)
        .with_name("orders-service")
        .with_timeout_ms(10_000),
).await?;
```

Trellis resolves deployment/instance assignment, installed participant/APIs,
`GrantBinding`, resources, signed context, route JWT, and transport endpoints
server-side. Authorization state is process-memory-only and refreshes on
reconnect; there is no context-store parameter.

Register generated providers before `service.run().await`. The service lifecycle
supervises its request host and workers. `with_timeout_ms(...)` bounds bootstrap,
connect, and request operations.

Apps/agents use user-login credentials (login session ID plus session seed) and
perform context refresh before CONNECT. Devices retain their provisioned
identity seed and use generated activation/connect options. Do not substitute a
raw NATS URL/JWT or client-authored assignment for either lifecycle.

## Typed Surfaces

Use the participant's generated methods. Dependency aliases are accessors on
`client()`; owned provider registration is under `handle()`. For the tutorial's
`orders` alias selecting RPC `Orders.Create`, use the generated
`connected.client().orders().orders_create(...)` method. Its argument type comes
from the generated API crate; it need not share the authored model's name.

Exact method and model names come from the generated crate. Match generated
declared-error variants directly; transport and unknown remote failures remain
distinct. Operations expose generated invokers and typed references for start,
wait, progress/watch, and optional cancellation/transfer.

Owned event publication uses `publisher()`. Durable listeners use declared
groups through `event_consumers()`; Trellis resolves their durable names and
authority. Retain the returned listener guard while delivery is needed; dropping
or aborting it removes that registration without stopping other registrations in
the group. The service lifecycle reports shared pull-loop failures.
Parameterized listeners match concrete subjects through their generated
subscription patterns and verify each event with its matching registration.
Unmatched messages are not acknowledged as completed work. Options select a
declared group, mode, and concurrency, not a custom durable name. Delivery may
repeat, so choose a side-effect strategy that handles duplicates.

Jobs are private service queues. Use generated queue handles and cloneable
`jobs_client()` handles for submission from other handlers. Worker registration
and processing are supervised by the service lifecycle. Jobs expose durable
state, retries, progress, cooperative cancellation, and optional live updates.

## Resources And Atomicity

Use the generated KV, store, State, and Jobs handles. Resolved binding payloads
and transport subjects are runtime internals. This does not restrict use of an
application-owned database or other storage system alongside Trellis.

Store readers/writers support bounded streaming through `write_from` and
`read_into`; whole-buffer helpers remain available. Transfer-capable operation
builders accept `transfer_from(reader, expected_size)`. Completion checks size
and SHA-256; cancellation is authenticated and acknowledged.

Prepared events and SQL outbox stores allow event intents to participate in a
local SQL transaction. The application owns its transaction and migration
execution. KV outbox/inbox stores do not atomically commit unrelated database
writes. See `/guides/libraries/rust` and current Rustdoc for supported stores
and transaction APIs.

SQL outbox claims expire after 30 seconds and can be reclaimed. Pass the claimed
record to `mark_published`/`mark_failed`; false means ownership was superseded.
`dispatch_outbox_once` returns `ClaimLost` for superseded completion.
Publication can repeat after interruption, so the claim fence is not
exactly-once delivery. Current schema helpers do not upgrade pre-release
layouts; applications own migration of any retained older database.

## Test And Verify

Run generation and the consuming project's own Cargo checks. A real-runtime test
can launch a Rust service from a Deno test using `@qlever-llc/trellis-test` and
its `TrellisTestRuntime`. This is a TypeScript helper, not a Rust crate API. A
Rust test can instead manage real runtime processes directly; Trellis does not
require one application test framework.

Use `/api` to discover current Rustdoc and generated participant source for
project-specific APIs. Private Trellis workspace crates are not consumer
dependencies. Trellis's supported Rust toolchain is current stable.
